title: P02 oxygen loss at 180-160 W continued to 2022 and matched phosphate gain; freshening limited water-type attribution
abstract: We tested oxygen and nutrient changes on P02 at 28-32 N and sigma0 26.3-26.7 in 2004, 2013 and 2022. Joint good-flag samples and common longitude-density support give a central 180-160 W oxygen loss of 6.48 umol/kg from 2013 to 2022 and 13.08 from 2004 to 2022. The endpoint AOU gain was 14.55 umol/kg. Phosphate rose by 0.0864, equal to 14.69 umol/kg of oxygen demand at a ratio of 170. The change in P - AOU/170 was 0.00084 (-0.00557 to 0.00780, conditional 95% spatial block interval). This agrees with accumulated respiration but does not separate ventilation, respiration rate or imported source changes. A local 2004 oxygen-salinity adjustment gives a larger central oxygen loss, but 94% of the central 2022 bin-density salinities are outside the 2004 range. Thus within-type attribution needs an untested extension of the reference relation. Nitrate does not close the same balance at nominal calibration. Three-degree bins and bottle salinity retain the raw central loss and phosphate balance. Strict interpolation leaves too little complete support. Only three occupations are used; cruise seasons, interpolation and calibration limit inference. Code, hashes, aggregate evidence and a separate numerical audit are included.

display.caption: Central AOU and phosphate changes match a respiration balance, while most central 2022 water types lie outside the 2004 salinity range. Intervals measure conditional spatial uncertainty and exclude calibration error.
